items.stimulus: A staffing agency pays a warehouse worker a base amount of \$80 per day plus \$12 for every 2 orders the worker packs that day.
items.stem: Which function $P$ gives the worker's pay, in dollars, for a day in which the worker packs $n$ orders?
items.explanation: The \$80 base is paid even when no orders are packed, so it is the constant term. The worker earns \$12 for every 2 orders, which is $12 \div 2 = 6$ dollars per order. So $P(n) = 80 + 6n$. To check, 2 orders give $80 + 12 = 92$, which is the base plus one \$12 payment, as the story says.

A.why: You used \$12 as the pay for each order, but \$12 is the pay for every 2 orders. You need to divide by 2 to get the rate for one order. With your function, 2 orders would earn \$24 instead of \$12.

B.why: You multiplied \$12 by 2 when you should have divided. Because the \$12 covers two orders, one order earns half of it, which is \$6, not \$24.

C.why: You swapped the base pay and the per-order rate. Your function pays \$6 for packing nothing and \$80 per order. The fixed \$80 should be the constant term, and the \$6 per order should multiply $n$.

items.stimulus: A meteorologist launches a weather balloon carrying a temperature sensor. At the moment of launch, the sensor reads $22^\circ\text{C}$. As the balloon rises, the temperature it records drops by $3^\circ\text{C}$ for every $500$ meters of altitude it gains. The function $T$ gives the temperature, in degrees Celsius, recorded by the sensor when the balloon is $h$ kilometers above the launch site.
items.stem: What is $T(3)$?
items.explanation: Start with the value when the input is 0. At $h = 0$ the sensor reads $22$, so that is the constant term. Next, find the rate per single unit of the input. The input is in kilometers, but the drop is given per $500$ meters. One kilometer is two lots of $500$ meters, so the temperature drops $2 \times 3 = 6$ degrees per kilometer. The temperature is falling, so the rate is negative: $T(h) = 22 - 6h$. Then $T(3) = 22 - 18 = 4$.

items.stimulus: A printmaking studio charges a one-time $\$90$ fee to prepare an etching plate. It then charges $\$14$ per print for each of the first 20 prints and $\$9$ per print for each print beyond 20.
items.stem: Which equation gives the total charge $C$, in dollars, for an edition of $n$ prints, where $n > 20$?
items.explanation: The fixed part is $90 + 14(20) = 370$ dollars for the setup fee and the first 20 prints. Only the $n - 20$ prints beyond those cost $\$9$ each. So $C = 370 + 9(n - 20) = 9n - 180 + 370 = 9n + 190$.
